newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Oil firms review Cambodian operations, investments.
newsitem.headline: Oil firms review Cambodian operations, investments.

text.p: Foreign oil firms in Cambodia, whose petrol stations have been shelled and looted, are putting their operations on hold and reviewing future investments, industry sources said on Tuesday.

The companies include state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT), Japanese trader Marubeni International Petroleum Co (MIPCO), France's Total SA and Caltex, a Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp joint venture.
Heavy fighting rocked the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh over the weekend, leaving forces loyal to Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen in control of the city and the government.
Rival First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, now in France, has vowed to resist.
"All I know is that our investment now is different from what it was a week ago," John Raeside, Caltex Cambodia's general manager told Reuters by telephone.
"We have a major commitment to the country and we will obviously put some of our investment commitment on hold until the situation becomes a bit clearer because we have no idea
whether the current happenings will receive condemnation from overseas."
Caltex will "generally follow through" on its existing $20-million investments and "is not considering pulling out at this moment," he said.
"But future investments have a question mark on them."
Cambodia is a small energy user compared to many Asian countries. But its potential for huge growth is attracting some of the world's biggest oil companies.
Cambodia's annual diesel and gasoline imports are 600,000-700,000 tonnes and are expected to grow 10 percent a year.
Caltex has 13 petrol stations and two convenience stores in Cambodia. It is halfway through an $8-million development of a marine terminal in the southern deep-sea port of Sihanoukville.
A Caltex convenience store and a service station at the airport has been ripped apart and looted, Raeside said.
A Total marketing executive in Phnom Penh, said one of its petrol stations has been "completely destroyed."
Total has 20 petrol stations in Cambodia--six in Phnom Penh and the rest in the provinces. Plans build 10 more stations were now under review, the executive said.
"It depends on whether the new stations will be in Phnom Penh or the provinces and what the situation will be there, they may be at war for two more years," he said.
A Total 8,000-cubic metre storage depot 20 kilomtres (12 miles) outside Phnom Penh is intact and operating normally.

PTT has shut its representative office and suspended operations in Cambodia indefinitely after repatriating its two Thai officials, said a director in charge of PTT International's Indochina operations.
"Our investments have to be reviewed," he said.
PTT's investments in Cambodia total 100 million baht and include seven petrol stations and a storage depot at the airport for aircraft refuelling, he said.

MIPCO, Marubeni Corp's trading arm, has suspended talks with Sokimex, Cambodia's biggest private oil marketing firm, for the $2-$3 million expansion of oil product storage in Sihanoukville to 50,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 30,000 bpd, a company official said.
MIPCO has also put on hold the delivery of an oil product cargo for delivery in July to Cambodia until fighting stops.
Its long-term plan to build a retail network with Sokimex, costing several million dollars, was to be reviewed. Sokimex has the most number of retail outlets in Cambodia with 220 stations.
-- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
